analysis.text: The Strong residential demand score reflects a substantial estimated resident base within the modelled walking areas. It is a residential opportunity indicator, not evidence of coffee purchases or current daytime demand.

The Moderate competition score tempers that opportunity. Potential coffee alternatives are recorded, while access remains conditional and the premises unresolved; none of these findings establishes a winning operating format.

test.text: Keep the site shortlisted but withhold lease commitment. Resolve layout, permissions, frontage demand and occupancy terms before deciding whether any coffee format is supportable.

pages.conclusion: Repeat local visits are the clearest demand hypothesis; weekday coffee demand still needs direct testing.

analysis.text: The cumulative walking estimates contain about 5,200 residents within five minutes, about 18,000 within ten and about 40,000 within fifteen. These overlapping, area-allocated Census estimates must not be added or treated as present-day customers.
Modelled annual household income of about £39,000 provides native-area context, not a coffee spending budget. It does not establish willingness to pay for premium drinks or regular food purchases.
The employment observation of about 350 employee jobs cannot fill the daytime evidence gap. Worker routines, visitor demand and the share passing this frontage are unverified.

test.text: Test morning convenience, weekday breaks and weekend repeat visits at the frontage. If those occasions are weak, the residential score alone should not justify the lease.

analysis.text: The nearby alternatives provide leads for checking coffee overlap. Their current trading status, customer appeal, prices and service periods are unknown.

Competition is about convenience as well as drinks. Check whether alternatives already meet quick takeaway, coffee with food and seated catch-up needs; missing reviews or brand details are not evidence of weak operators.

No complete unique competitor total is established. Native mapped records and the food register have different coverage and may include duplicates, historical entries or businesses with little coffee overlap.

test.text: Visit verified alternatives and compare the same customer occasions. If their convenience, food and seating already cover the proposed offer, require a demonstrable difference before progressing.

pages.conclusion: Walking accessibility is useful context, but frontage convenience and passing coffee demand remain unverified.

analysis.text: The retained walking areas model routes from a recorded building point or postcode centre. They do not verify the entrance, pedestrian flow, visibility or whether a station approach brings customers past the counter.

A takeaway-led offer would depend on an easy stop and reliable service speed. Balanced or sit-in coffee would also need convenient access for repeat visits; neither advantage is established by the routing evidence.

test.text: Walk the actual approach to the entrance and observe stopping behaviour at relevant trading times. An awkward diversion or weak frontage flow would reduce the convenience case and require stronger repeat-visit evidence.

pages.conclusion: No coffee format is yet verified as physically or legally workable, so lease commitment must remain withheld.

analysis.text: Takeaway-led coffee needs workable counter, queue, preparation, washing and storage space. Balanced and sit-in alternatives also depend on seating, circulation and suitable facilities; capacity is not established.

The designation search returned about 2 Article 4 records and about 0 conservation-area records. These are provider search outcomes, not confirmation of applicability, permitted use or planning clearance.
The point rivers-and-sea observation is Very Low, but it does not cover surface water, the full premises or overall property risk. It cannot replace condition and property checks.

test.text: Have the measured plan and proposed activities checked against permissions, lease restrictions and facilities. A contrary finding could remove a format or the site itself; do not infer approval from provider classification.

pages.conclusion: The rent evidence is a restaurant asking benchmark, not an established rent or affordability case for this coffee shop.

analysis.text: The supplied modelled restaurant benchmark is about £30 per square foot per year on an NIA basis. It is not the selected unit's asking rent and should not be presented as a retail coffee-shop cohort.

Source date, model vintage, dispersion and selected-format comparability are unresolved, and the search-radius units are unspecified. The benchmark therefore offers limited negotiating context rather than a firm valuation.

test.text: Obtain the actual rent and full lease liabilities, then compare current coffee-suitable premises on a consistent area basis. Poor comparability or onerous terms would require renegotiation or withdrawal.

cautions.text: Local asking-rent context is not a contracted lease, and an unknown source date or radius limits comparability. Do not multiply an NIA benchmark by a GIA floor area.

pages.conclusion: Resolve the premises gate first, then test demand, alternatives and occupancy terms before making a lease decision.

analysis.text: Keep the operating comparison open. Fast takeaway depends on convenient flow and queue space; balanced or sit-in coffee depends on a usable seating offer and repeat occasions. None is the verified winner.

The decision should change with the checks, not merely accumulate reassurance. Failed permissions, weak customer occasions, strong offer overlap or unsuitable lease terms could each undermine the shortlist.

test.text: Revisit the conditional shortlist only after the plan, permissions, frontage observations, competitor checks and actual lease terms are available. Until then, withhold lease commitment.

verdict: The residential demand score is Strong and the competition score is Moderate. These support further investigation, not a sales forecast: worker, visitor and passing demand remain unverified.

Withhold lease commitment until the unit's layout, permitted activities and lease conditions are verified. Takeaway-led, balanced and sit-in coffee remain conditional alternatives, with no verified leading format.

strengths.text: The residential base gives repeat coffee visits a credible testing ground. The modelled five-minute walking area contains about 5,200 residents, although this is an area-allocated Census estimate rather than current customers.

The wider residential setting could support weekend coffee and food occasions. The ten-minute walking estimate includes about 2,700 residents aged 25–29; their coffee preferences and purchasing are unmeasured.

risks.text: Premises uncertainty is the immediate commitment risk. Usable layout, permitted activities, condition and lease terms are unresolved, so neither seating capacity nor a workable service format is established.

A strong residential score does not establish a busy morning counter. The retained employment context records about 350 employee jobs in its native area, not visitors or frontage footfall; daytime conversion remains unknown.

Coffee alternatives could constrain repeat visits despite the Moderate competition score. The register contains potential competitors, but current trading, prices, service speed and food or seating offers are unverified.
The available rent benchmark is for restaurants, not a verified comparable coffee unit. Selected-unit rent and lease liabilities are unknown, so occupancy affordability cannot yet be judged.

summary.priority: Obtain a measured usable plan, written confirmation of permitted coffee-shop activities and the draft lease. Test queueing, preparation, washing, storage, seating and customer facilities before choosing a format or committing.

actions.action: Verify the exact trading unit, usable layout, permitted activities and lease restrictions. Compare takeaway-led, balanced and sit-in coffee against the same plan rather than treating missing seating evidence as a takeaway recommendation.
actions.consequence: A workable layout and confirmed permissions would allow format selection. Inadequate preparation space, circulation or permissions could require redesign or rejection; lease commitment should remain withheld until resolved.

actions.action: Observe the actual frontage during morning, weekday daytime and weekend periods. Walk the proposed station approach and ask local customers about repeat coffee, food and seating needs.
actions.consequence: Consistent convenient passing trade would strengthen the case for fast service. Weak frontage flow would shift attention to proven local repeat visits and destination appeal, or undermine the site if neither is evident.

actions.action: Verify nearby coffee alternatives, starting with Little Lantern Café and Elm & Ember. Check current identity, opening periods, prices, queues, food and seating, and exclude the selected unit from the comparison.
actions.consequence: A genuine gap in speed, opening periods or food and seating could support a differentiated offer. Strong overlap would weaken the commercial case even if the residential catchment remains attractive.

actions.action: Obtain the selected unit's asking rent, measured area, service charges, rates position, repair obligations and fit-out requirements. Seek current coffee-suitable comparables separately from the supplied restaurant cohort.
actions.consequence: Verified occupancy terms would make an affordability review meaningful. Unfavourable liabilities or weak comparable support would justify renegotiation or withdrawal rather than relying on the area benchmark.
